A limit the page states about itself. Still true: the ten clocks all come from this site.

Template arithmetic is right: ratio = longer days / shorter days; "if the short one were a single day" gives ratio days, or ratio/365 years above 1,000. Example: 168,995 / 2 = 84,498 times, about 231 years.

Nine of ten clocks match home. The Crozer bar does not: it reads "Court order · counted from 8 June 2026 · 269 days". Home methodology: "Day count to March 2, 2027 was computed from today (June 6, 2026): 269 days." 8 June 2026 to 2 March 2027 is 267 days; 6 June is 269. (The brief is dated 10 June and also says "269 days from today", which would be 265.) On 10 November 2026, 112 days remain.

Arithmetic, each bar: 2 days OK (two business days counted as two calendar days). 62 days OK (31 Aug to 1 Nov 2022). 269 days WRONG for the stated start date (see c004). 13 months = 395 OK (13 x 30.4 = 395.2). 4 years = 1,460 OK. 8 years = 2,920 OK. 5,142 days = 14.09 years OK. 15 years = 5,475 OK. 50 years = 18,250 OK. 463 years = 168,995 OK (463 x 365).

Allegheny: 18 May 2012 to 15 June 2026 (the brief's date) is 5,141 days; 5,142 falls on 16 June. One day off at home, inside the remix's "as of June 2026". The brief's counter is live and now shows more.
Parish registers: home dates the rule to 11 November 1563, so the 463rd year completes on 11 November 2026, one day after this page's date. Rounding, not an error.

Room 2 headline (untagged): "The clocks that protect you are the short ones." The wall's own HIPAA bar is a 50-year protection for the person. The tagged INFERENCE (c001) is worded more carefully; the headline says more than the wall shows.

North Carolina: home says reappraisal "at least every eight years", a maximum. The bar's "How often ... must reassess · 8 years" is acceptable. S&P 500: home says "about fifteen years, by Innosight's count"; the bar says "Innosight estimate · 15 years".
